concept.name: Docker Images & Layers

relationships.description: Connects Docker Images & Layers to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: A Docker image is an immutable stack of content-addressable filesystem tarballs (layers) merged at runtime via a copy-on-write union filesystem like OverlayFS.
spark.keyTakeaway: Order Dockerfile instructions from least-frequently changed to most-frequently changed, combine `RUN` cleanup in the same layer, and use multi-stage builds so build toolchains never ship to production.

concept.whyItMatters: Every `RUN`, `COPY`, and `ADD` instruction creates a new read-only layer identified by its SHA-256 diff digest. Poor layer hygiene bloats images from 40 MB to 1.8 GB, busts BuildKit layer caches on every commit, and slows Kubernetes pod cold-starts across nodes.
whenToUse: Packaging microservices with predictable dependencies so CI/CD builds reuse cached base and dependency layers across commits.
Distributing multi-architecture (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) OCI artifacts where registry pulls deduplicate shared base layers by digest.
Isolating build-time compilers (GCC, Maven, Node `devDependencies`) in a builder stage before copying only compiled binaries into a minimal runtime stage.
whenNotToUse: Storing mutable application state, database files, or user uploads inside the container writable `upperdir` instead of external volumes.
Baking environment-specific secrets (`.env`, TLS private keys, AWS credentials) into `ENV` or `COPY` layers where `docker history` and tar extraction expose them permanently.
Running monolithic legacy workloads that require full systemd init trees and mutable host kernel modules rather than a single-process container.
keyPoints: OverlayFS mounts read-only image layers as `lowerdir`, a container-specific writable layer as `upperdir`, and presents the unified view at `merged`.
Deleting a file from a lower layer in a subsequent `RUN rm` instruction only writes a whiteout file (`.wh.<filename>`) in the upper layer—it does not shrink the lower layer's registry size.
BuildKit evaluates cache invalidation top-down: once a `COPY . .` layer changes, every downstream `RUN` instruction misses cache and re-executes.
Multi-stage builds (`FROM golang:1.23 AS builder` -> `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot`) cut image surface area and CVE count by omitting shells, package managers, and headers.

OCI Image Manifests (`application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json`) separate compressed layer blobs (`diff_ids` vs compressed digests) so registries skip transferring layers already cached on the host.

examples.title: Python FastAPI service slimmed via multi-stage + cache mount
examples.scenario: A FastAPI service initially used `FROM python:3.12` (1.02 GB) with `COPY . .` before `pip install -r requirements.txt`, causing 4-minute CI rebuilds on every single-line code edit.
examples.outcome: Switching to `COPY requirements.txt .` before `pip install` with `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip` and copying the virtualenv into `python:3.12-slim` cut image size to 168 MB and dropped incremental CI build time to 9 seconds.

examples.title: Eliminating leaked secrets and bloated apt cache
examples.scenario: An engineer ran `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl` in one layer and `RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` in the next layer, alongside `COPY .npmrc /root/.npmrc` followed by `RUN rm /root/.npmrc`.
examples.outcome: Inspecting the image tarballs revealed both `/var/lib/apt/lists` (38 MB) and the `.npmrc` auth token remained recoverable in earlier layers. Combining cleanup into one `RUN` and using `--mount=type=secret,id=npmrc` removed both the bloat and the credential leak.

tradeOffs.factor: Base image minimalism (Distroless / Alpine vs Debian Slim)
tradeOffs.pro: Distroless (`~20 MB`) and Alpine (`~7 MB`) minimize registry transfer time and eliminate shell-based RCE primitives.
tradeOffs.con: Alpine's `musl` libc can trigger DNS resolution quirks or wheel compilation failures for Python/C++ binaries, while Distroless lacks `sh`/`curl` for ad-hoc `kubectl exec` debugging (requiring ephemeral debug containers).

tradeOffs.pro: Chaining related commands into fewer `RUN` layers reduces overlayfs metadata overhead and ensures temporary files deleted in the same step never persist.
tradeOffs.con: Over-consolidating unrelated steps into one giant `RUN` ruins BuildKit cache reuse when only one sub-step changes.

tradeOffs.pro: Collapses whiteouts and intermediate history into a single compact tarball for distribution.
tradeOffs.con: Destroys shared base-layer deduplication across services, forcing nodes to re-download the entire base OS on every minor app release.

failureModes.name: Cache busting from early `COPY . .`
failureModes.description: Copying the entire repository before installing dependencies invalidates package-manager layers whenever `README.md` or application source files change.
failureModes.mitigation: Copy only lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `poetry.lock`, `go.sum`) first, install dependencies, and `COPY` application source last; pair with `.dockerignore` excluding `.git`, `node_modules`, and `tests/`.

failureModes.name: Phantom size from cross-layer deletion
failureModes.description: Downloading a 500 MB SDK tarball in `RUN curl ...` and removing it in a separate `RUN rm` leaves the 500 MB blob permanently inside the image manifest.
failureModes.mitigation: Chain download, extraction, and deletion inside a single `RUN` command (`&& rm -rf ...`) or use BuildKit `RUN --mount=type=bind` / multi-stage `COPY --from`.

failureModes.name: OverlayFS copy-up latency on heavy writes
failureModes.description: Modifying a large pre-existing file (e.g., an SQLite DB or 200 MB log) in `lowerdir` forces OverlayFS to copy the entire file up to `upperdir` on first write.
failureModes.mitigation: Mount external volumes (`-v` or Kubernetes `emptyDir`/`PVC`) for any directory receiving runtime writes so I/O bypasses OverlayFS copy-up.

failureModes.name: Floating `:latest` tag drift
failureModes.description: Pinning `FROM node:20` or `:latest` causes builds on Tuesday to pull a different OS/OpenSSL patch layer than builds on Monday, breaking reproducibility.
failureModes.mitigation: Pin base images by immutable SHA-256 digest (`FROM node:20.18.0-slim@sha256:...`) and automate bumps via Renovate or Dependabot.

commonMistakes: Forgetting `.dockerignore`, which sends `.git/` (hundreds of MB) and local `.env` files into the BuildKit build context.
Running `apt-get update` in its own `RUN` layer, causing stale package index caches to fail `apt-get install` months later.
Assuming `USER nonroot` at the end of a Dockerfile changes ownership of files already `COPY`'d as `root` without `--chown=nonroot:nonroot`.
Using `ADD` with remote URLs instead of `curl` + checksum verification, or unintentionally auto-extracting tarballs.
Leaving `pip`, `npm`, or `apt` caches inside the final layer instead of mounting `--mount=type=cache` during build.

sections.content:
## The idea

A Docker (OCI) image is not a monolithic VM disk—it is a JSON manifest pointing to an ordered stack of immutable, gzip/zstd-compressed filesystem tarballs called **layers**. Each layer captures only the filesystem delta (added, modified, or whiteout-deleted files) introduced by a single `RUN`, `COPY`, or `ADD` instruction.

At container startup, the container runtime (`containerd` + `runc`) does not copy those gigabytes of layers. Instead, it instructs the Linux kernel's **OverlayFS** driver to stack the read-only layers as `lowerdir`, attach a fresh, empty read-write directory as `upperdir`, and expose the combined filesystem at `merged`. Because lower layers are strictly read-only and addressed by their SHA-256 content digest, ten containers on the same host share one physical copy of the OS and runtime layers in page cache.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider building a Go HTTP service with BuildKit (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1`):
1. `FROM golang:1.23-alpine@sha256:... AS builder` pulls 3 base layers (~85 MB compressed) once and caches them locally.
2. `WORKDIR /src` and `COPY go.mod go.sum ./` create tiny metadata/file layers. If `go.mod` hasn't changed since yesterday, BuildKit hits cache.
3. `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download` populates Go's module cache on a persistent BuildKit cache volume without baking downloaded module tarballs into the image layer.
4. `COPY . .` + `RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/server ./cmd/server` compiles a static ELF binary.
5. `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` starts stage 2, and `COPY --from=builder /out/server /server` copies only the 14 MB binary.

When `docker push` runs, the registry checks each layer's SHA-256 digest via `HEAD /v2/<repo>/blobs/<digest>`, skips uploading the unchanged `distroless` base layers, and uploads only the new 14 MB binary layer.

sections.content:
## BuildKit cache mechanics & multi-stage patterns

Modern Docker builds rely on **BuildKit**, which builds a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of instructions rather than executing a linear script. Independent stages in a multi-stage Dockerfile execute in parallel, and unused stages are skipped entirely unless targeted.

Two BuildKit mount flags eliminate layer bloat without sacrificing speed:
- `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip` keeps package-manager caches across builds on the builder host without writing a single byte into the final image layer.
- `--mount=type=secret,id=github_token` exposes credentials at `/run/secrets/github_token` only during that `RUN` step, leaving zero trace in `docker history` or layer tarballs.

## Base image & layer strategy comparison

| Strategy | Typical Size | Shell / Pkg Mgr | CVE Surface | Best Fit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Full OS (`ubuntu:24.04`, `python:3.12`) | 800 MB – 1.2 GB | `bash`, `apt`, `gcc` | High (100+ packages) | Local devcontainers, builder stages only |
| Slim (`debian:bookworm-slim`, `python:3.12-slim`) | 75 MB – 180 MB | `sh`, `apt` (minimal) | Medium | Python/Node apps needing `glibc` compatibility |
| Alpine (`alpine:3.20`) | 7 MB – 50 MB | `ash`, `apk` | Very Low | Static Go/Rust binaries or pure-JS Node services |
| Distroless (`gcr.io/distroless/static`) | 2 MB – 25 MB | None | Minimal | Production Go, Rust, Java (`distroless/java21`) |

## Failure modes

1. **Whiteout bloat (`rm` in a later layer)**: Running `rm -rf /tmp/sdk` in a separate `RUN` creates a `.wh.sdk` marker in the upper layer while the lower layer still ships the full SDK over the network.
2. **Copy-up stalls**: Writing to a 500 MB pre-seeded database file inside `lowerdir` forces OverlayFS to synchronously copy all 500 MB into `upperdir` before the first byte mutates.
3. **Context explosion**: Omitting `.dockerignore` causes `docker build` to tar `node_modules` or `.git` on every run, adding 30–60 seconds before instruction 1 even starts.
4. **Layer limit & inode exhaustion**: Exceeding ~125 layers degrades OverlayFS lookup latency, while unpacked `node_modules` trees with 100,000+ tiny files can exhaust host `ext4`/`xfs` inodes.

## Inspecting and auditing layers

Treat image size and layer contents as CI gate metrics:
- Run `dive <image:tag>` locally or in CI (`CI=true dive <image>`) to inspect exact wasted bytes, duplicate files across layers, and layer efficiency percentages (aim for `>95%`).
- Use `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>` to verify multi-arch manifest lists and confirm compressed layer sizes.
- Scan final runtime images—not builder images—with `trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL <image>` so CVEs in build-only compilers don't create alert fatigue.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Add a strict `.dockerignore` excluding `.git`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `target/`, `__pycache__/`, and test fixtures.
- [ ] Pin base images with explicit version tags and SHA-256 digests (`@sha256:...`).
- [ ] Copy dependency manifests (`package-lock.json`, `go.sum`, `requirements.txt`) before application source code.
- [ ] Use `RUN --mount=type=cache` for package managers and `RUN --mount=type=secret` for private registry tokens.
- [ ] Separate compile/build toolchains into an `AS builder` stage and ship only runtime artifacts into `slim` or `distroless`.
- [ ] Run containers as an explicit non-root UID (`USER 65532:65532`) with `COPY --chown`.

interviewProblems.title: Docker Images & Layers
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Docker Images & Layers. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: A Docker image is an immutable stack of content-addressable filesystem tarballs (layers) merged at runtime via a copy-on-write union filesystem like OverlayFS.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: OverlayFS Union applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Running Container.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Running Container experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Copy only lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `poetry.lock`, `go.sum`) first, install dependencies, and `COPY` application source last; pair with `.dockerignore` excluding `.git`, `node_modules`, and `tests/`.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Order Dockerfile instructions from least-frequently changed to most-frequently changed, combine `RUN` cleanup in the same layer, and use multi-stage builds so build toolchains never ship to production.
Avoid trap: Forgetting `.dockerignore`, which sends `.git/` (hundreds of MB) and local `.env` files into the BuildKit build context.
Avoid trap: Running `apt-get update` in its own `RUN` layer, causing stale package index caches to fail `apt-get install` months later.
When to reach for it: Packaging microservices with predictable dependencies so CI/CD builds reuse cached base and dependency layers across commits.
When to reach for it: Distributing multi-architecture (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) OCI artifacts where registry pulls deduplicate shared base layers by digest.

putItTogether.title: Putting Docker Image Layers Together
putItTogether.summary: Order Dockerfile instructions from least-frequently changed to most-frequently changed, combine `RUN` cleanup in the same layer, and use multi-stage builds so build toolchains never ship to production.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Docker Image Layers before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Switching to `COPY requirements.txt .` before `pip install` with `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip` and copying the virtualenv into `python:3.12-slim` cut image size to 168 MB and dropped incremental CI build time to 9 seconds.
